statement: Whenever min_interval(intervals, queries) returns a result r, len(r) = m and for every j with 0 <= j < m: if there exists i with 0 <= i < n and intervals[i][0] <= queries[j] <= intervals[i][1], then r[j] = min { intervals[i][1] - intervals[i][0] + 1 | 0 <= i < n and intervals[i][0] <= queries[j] <= intervals[i][1] }; otherwise r[j] = -1.
preconditions: Let n = len(intervals) and m = len(queries). The input satisfies: 1 <= n <= 100000, 1 <= m <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(intervals[i]) = 2, and writing intervals[i][0] and intervals[i][1] for its entries, 1 <= intervals[i][0] <= intervals[i][1] <= 10000000; for every j with 0 <= j < m, 1 <= queries[j] <= 10000000.
